vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-workspace-cleaner
Version: 1.0.1

The workspace-cleaner skill is a maintenance utility designed to optimize the agent's workspace by archiving redundant information and deleting obsolete files like BOOTSTRAP.md. It includes built-in safety protocols, such as requiring explicit user confirmation before executing any changes and restricting its operations to the agent's own directory. No indicators of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or unauthorized access were found in SKILL.md or _meta.json.

llm.summary: Instruction-only workspace cleanup that is broadly coherent with its stated purpose but contains metadata mismatches and relies on unenforced runtime constraints (file-scope safety), so proceed with caution and verify before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the instructions: the skill reads, prunes, archives, and deletes workspace bootstrap files. It requires no binaries, credentials, or external services — those are appropriate for a local workspace-cleaner. However the package _meta.json (ownerId/version) disagrees with the registry metadata provided, which is unexpected and should be investigated.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to read and modify workspace files (MEMORY.md, SOUL.md, AGENTS.md, TOOLS.md, IDENTITY.md, USER.md, BOOTSTRAP.md) and to archive content under memory/. That is aligned with the purpose but carries risk: the safety constraints ("only modify your own workspace", "don't touch other agents' files") are advisory text — there is no technical enforcement in the instructions. The skill also deletes files (BOOTSTRAP.md) and appends to existing archive files, which are destructive operations. The skill does require explicit user confirmation before executing, which mitigates risk if the human reviews the proposed changes carefully.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files; nothing is downloaded or written by an installer. This minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No environment variables, credentials, or config paths are requested — appropriate for a local file-cleaner. No unrelated secrets are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no persistence/install steps. disable-model-invocation is false (default) which allows autonomous invocation; this is the platform default and not by itself a disqualifying risk, but combined with the ability to modify files it increases blast radius if the agent is overly autonomous.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's behavior is broadly consistent with its stated goal, but take precautions before allowing it to run: 1) Investigate the metadata mismatch: the _meta.json ownerId/version differ from the registry metadata — ask the publisher which is authoritative. 2) Request the analysis/diff (the SKILL.md promises a proposed change list) and review it carefully before saying "可以"/"执行"; do not approve blindly. 3) Back up your workspace (or run in a sandbox/clone) before executing — the skill may delete BOOTSTRAP.md and append/alter files. 4) Verify the agent will operate only on the intended directory (check working directory and file paths) because the instructions rely on an honor system to avoid touching other agents' files. 5) If you plan to allow autonomous invocation, consider revoking that right until you’ve safely tested the skill. 6) Prefer a dry-run mode and insist the agent produce explicit file-level diffs and target archive paths before making changes.
